rationale: Iteration 0 has no race data or evaluator feedback, so this is a conservative baseline built from the contract. Geometry: five line sensors spaced 10 mm apart across x = -0.02 to +0.02 m, placed 50 mm ahead of the axle so they read the line before the wheels reach it. A 12 mm footprint is wider than the 10 mm spacing, so the sensors overlap and the signal stays smooth on the 25 mm tape. The wheel track (0.12 m), radius (0.03 m), mass (0.8 kg) and body dimensions are mid-range values that keep yaw inertia moderate. Controller: a symmetric weight pattern (-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1) gives a signal in [-1, 1]. kp = 4 gives a moderate steering response (about 1400 PWM difference at full signal). kd = 0.3 damps overshoot on the bends, and ki = 0.05 is small so the integral does not wind up on the long curves. base_speed = 1.6 (about 80% PWM) is chosen to reach the roughly 1.5 m/s average needed to finish in 3 s while leaving headroom for the slalom and tight bends. line_loss = last_direction so that a momentary loss turns the robot back toward the line it came from. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend, with some oscillation on the slalom. The next race should show whether speed or steering gain is the limit. Hypotheses: (1) kp is too low for the slalom and progress stalls; (2) base_speed of 1.6 is too fast for the tightest bend, causing line loss. Measurements requested: completion, progress, completion time, rms and max error, line-loss events and steering jitter.
